where_to_look_first.flowering: Start with inflorescence architecture, then isolate one spikelet and inspect glumes, florets, lemma/palea, awns/bristles and attachment.
where_to_look_first.vegetative: Go directly to the collar region where blade meets sheath. Pull the blade gently away from the culm and inspect ligule, auricles, collar, sheath, hairs and node.

family_characters: Culms are jointed into nodes and internodes; internodes are commonly hollow or pith-filled, while nodes are solid.
Leaves are typically 2-ranked and consist of sheath + blade with a collar region at their junction.
The sheath usually wraps around the culm and is commonly open/split rather than completely fused.
A ligule is commonly present at the inner blade-sheath junction; it may be membranous, hairy, very short or occasionally absent.
Auricles may be present or absent and can be highly diagnostic when present.
The basic reproductive unit is the spikelet.
One or two glumes usually occur at the base of a spikelet; each floret is typically enclosed by a lemma and palea.
Awns or bristles may arise from spikelet/floret structures and are often diagnostic.
The fruit is a caryopsis (grain), with the seed coat fused to the fruit wall.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not assume every grass has a hollow round internode; flattened or pith-filled culms occur.
Do not identify grasses by leaf width or color alone.
Do not call every grass-like plant Poaceae; sedges and rushes require explicit comparison.
Do not wait for seedheads if vegetative collar characters are available.

Poaceae.stem: Usually round/flattened, jointed, with obvious nodes; internodes often hollow.
Poaceae.key_confirmation: Nodes + collar region; reproductive units are spikelets with glumes and florets.

Cyperaceae.stem: Usually solid and often triangular; no grass-like jointed nodes.
Cyperaceae.key_confirmation: Triangular solid culm plus sedge spike/scale architecture; Carex uses perigynia.

Juncaceae.stem: Usually round and solid, without obvious grass nodes.
Juncaceae.key_confirmation: Small but recognizable flowers commonly with 6 tepals and a capsule rather than grass spikelets.

local_practice_groups.note: Use curated Bothriochloa torreyana and Schizachyrium scoparium as anchors.

look_for: distinct comb/flag-like spike branches or reduced specialized heads
Aristida typically 3 awns vs Nassella one conspicuous twisted awn
